title: Tarnbrook Health — a virtual desktop rollout that limps

tabs.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Tarnbrook Health runs community clinics across two regions and moved 2,400 clinical and administrative staff onto Azure Virtual Desktop nine months ago. Clinicians work from shared consulting-room devices and from home; a smaller group of imaging specialists needs local administrator rights and software that will not run multi-session.
The deployment works but is disliked. A review has produced the findings below, and the infrastructure team has been asked to fix them before the second region goes live.

tabs.heading: Existing environment
paragraphs: Profile containers sit on a general-purpose storage account using standard storage. Sign-in takes between 90 seconds and four minutes, and the Insights profile load time counter is consistently the largest component. Defender Antivirus is running with default settings on every session host.

A batch of forty new session hosts was built last week from a captured image. None of them registered with the host pool. The image was captured directly from a running virtual machine after the applications were installed.
A newly onboarded department was assigned to an application group and reports that nothing appears in their client feed at all. The assignment is present and correct when checked.

Clinicians connect from home over consumer broadband and describe the session as laggy when scrolling and typing. Round-trip time measured from those homes averages 60 ms, and the host pool's processor and memory counters are unremarkable during the complaints.
The imaging specialists are currently in the same pooled host pool as everyone else. Their software fails intermittently and they cannot install their own tools.
Every session host in the pool runs continuously. Utilisation between 19:00 and 07:00 is close to zero, and the monthly compute bill has been raised at board level.
Microsoft 365 Apps were installed into the image with a standard installation. Users report activation prompts and, on some hosts, Office refusing to open.

tabs.heading: Requirements
paragraphs: Sign-in time must be reduced, and the storage tier must be appropriate for profile containers rather than merely cheap.
Newly built session hosts must register with the host pool reliably.
The newly onboarded department must see their desktop in the client feed.
The lag clinicians describe must be addressed at the connection layer, given that round-trip time is acceptable and the hosts are not overloaded.
The imaging specialists must have a dedicated machine each, with local administrator rights and software that cannot run multi-session.
Compute spend outside working hours must fall without staff losing access when they do connect.
Microsoft 365 Apps must activate correctly on multi-session hosts.
